messages:
ritesh_cust: Hey team, urgent — our compliance folks cannot view Audit Logs in the Compliance UI after SSO sign-in. They get a "You don't have permission to view audit logs" modal. This is blocking our audit. We're on Okta SSO, role mapped to `ComplianceViewer` via `groups` claim. Can someone escalate? (org: redwood-ops, ticket #12345)

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you confirm if the error is in the UI only or also when hitting the audit API directly? Any console/network errors/screenshots would help. Also what exact SSO provider + attribute mapping are you using?

ritesh_cust: UI + API. Screenshot attached: https://files.example.com/snap_001.png. Tried Chrome incognito and Safari. They can see other logs but audit logs older than ~30 days are missing. We expect 365d retention. SSO: Okta, groups claim.

alex_support: thx. Can you paste the raw API response from a failing request (curl response or network tab)? e.g. `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/logs?start=..."` or run `POST /v1/debug/whoami` to confirm token scopes.

ritesh_cust: Pasted from network: 
```json
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "insufficient_scope",
  "message": "token missing required scope: audit.read"
}
```

alex_support: OK that explains a lot — token doesn't include `audit.read`. @maria_se can you check the SSO -> session token mapping? Also we should verify entitlement that controls retention (audit.retention).

maria_se: I'm looking. I was able to reproduce locally with Okta SAML assertion. The SAML -> JWT translation service dropped `entitlement` claims when the IdP used `groups` instead of an `entitlement` attribute. There's a regression introduced in config parsing in the release on 2026-02-18. I've opened ENG ticket RNW-8721. Root cause: fallback logic to map `groups` -> `entitlements` was removed in the token-minting service.

infra_oncall: Immediate mitigations: either add an explicit `entitlement` attribute in Okta containing `audit.read` and `audit.retention:365`, or temporarily grant the role the audit entitlement from the Admin Console. Quick admin steps: 
1) Console -> Settings -> Entitlements -> Add `audit.read` to `ComplianceViewer`.
2) Or curl (org admin):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/entitlements \ 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \ 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
 -d '{"org":"redwood-ops","role":"ComplianceViewer","entitlements":["audit.read","audit.retention:365"]}'
```
Either one should restore access immediately.

alex_support: Can infra/eng push a hotfix so tokens minted from SSO regain `audit.read` automatically? RNW-8721 should track that. @jenna_pm tagging for customer comms.

ritesh_cust: Trying Admin Console change now, will report back in ~30m. Thanks.

--- (30 minutes later) ---

ritesh_cust: Confirmed — adding `audit.read` entitlement to `ComplianceViewer` in Admin Console fixed it. Compliance team can query historical logs now, retention appears as expected.

alex_support: Great. Closing customer ticket #12345 on our side, but RNW-8721 stays open until fix and tests land. Assigning to @maria_se.

maria_se: Assigned RNW-8721 to me. Adding unit + integration tests for SAML->JWT entitlement mapping. Target deploy window: tomorrow 02:00 UTC. I'll post deploybot updates when ready.

deploy_bot: deploy started: branch rnw/8721-fix-sso-entitlements to prod at 1801234780

deploy_bot: deploy success: prod @ 1801234845

alex_support: Confirmed post-deploy that SSO sessions now include `audit.read` scope and `audit.retention` claims where applicable. Closing this thread. :tada:
